treatment: Use well-drained soil and avoid waterlogging. Rotate with non-solanaceous crops.

description: Caused by Alternaria solani. Dark brown concentric rings (target-board pattern) on older leaves.
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicides. Ensure adequate potassium nutrition. Remove infected debris.

description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans (same pathogen as the Irish Famine). Water-soaked lesions with white mould on undersides.

treatment: Use certified seed tubers. Hill plants to prevent tuber greening.

description: Caused by Xanthomonas spp. Small, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves; scab-like spots on fruit.
treatment: Use copper-based bactericides. Avoid working in fields when wet. Use resistant varieties.

description: Caused by Alternaria solani. Dark concentric ring spots (bull's-eye) on older leaves. Causes defoliation.
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Stake plants for airflow. Practice crop rotation.

description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Irregular greasy lesions; white sporulation on undersides in humid conditions.
treatment: Apply metalaxyl or cymoxanil fungicides. Destroy infected material. Avoid planting near infected potato fields.

description: Caused by Passalora fulva. Pale green to yellow spots on upper surface; olive-green velvety mould below.
treatment: Improve greenhouse ventilation. Apply fungicides (chlorothalonil). Use resistant varieties.

description: Caused by Septoria lycopersici. Circular spots with grey centres and dark margins on lower leaves.
treatment: Remove lower infected leaves. Apply fungicides (mancozeb, chlorothalonil). Avoid overhead irrigation.

description: Tetranychus urticae infestation. Tiny yellow stippling on leaves; fine webbing on undersides; leaves become bronzed.
treatment: Apply miticides (abamectin, spiromesifen). Introduce predatory mites. Keep plants well-watered.

description: Caused by Corynespora cassiicola. Concentric ring lesions on leaves; dark spots on fruit.
treatment: Apply fungicides (azoxystrobin). Ensure good airflow. Remove infected debris.

description: Transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). Causes upward curling, yellowing and stunting of young leaves.
treatment: Control whitefly with insecticides or reflective mulches. Use resistant varieties. Remove infected plants.

description: Caused by Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV). Mosaic pattern of light/dark green on leaves; leaf distortion and stunting.
treatment: Use virus-free seed. Disinfect tools with bleach. Remove and destroy infected plants. Use resistant varieties.

description: A fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. Causes olive-green to brown scab-like lesions on leaves and fruit.
treatment: Apply fungicides (captan, myclobutanil) at bud break. Remove fallen leaves. Plant resistant varieties.

description: Caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. Produces frog-eye leaf spots and black, mummified fruit.
treatment: Prune infected wood. Apply copper-based fungicides. Destroy mummified fruit.

description: Caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Produces bright orange spots on leaves.
treatment: Remove nearby juniper hosts. Apply fungicides (mancozeb, myclobutanil) in spring.

treatment: Maintain proper soil pH (4.5–5.5) and regular pruning.

description: Caused by Podosphaera clandestina. White powdery growth on young leaves, shoots and fruit.

description: The cherry leaf shows no signs of disease or pest damage.
treatment: Prune annually to improve light and airflow. Fertilise in spring.

description: Caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis. Rectangular grey lesions with yellow halos running parallel to leaf veins.
treatment: Plant resistant hybrids. Rotate crops. Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides.

description: Caused by Puccinia sorghi. Small, cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Plant resistant hybrids. Apply foliar fungicides (propiconazole) if severe.

description: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum. Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions.

description: A complex trunk disease caused by wood-rotting fungi. Causes tiger-stripe leaf symptoms and berry spotting.

description: Caused by Pseudocercospora vitis. Dark brown irregular spots with yellow halos on leaves.
